title: USDA Lists Active New World Screwworm Case in Webb County
excerpt: The U.S. Department of Agriculture lists an active New World screwworm case in Webb County, involving livestock, after the Texas Animal Health Commission updated its infested zones to include Webb and Hidalgo counties, according to KGNS.
content:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture's online dashboard lists an active New World screwworm case in Webb County, according to KGNS.

The listing was posted Nov. 17, 2026, and involves livestock, the station reported. The Texas Animal Health Commission said it recently updated its infested zones after new cases in counties including Webb and Hidalgo.

Webb Watch previously reported confirmed screwworm cases in Starr and Zapata counties earlier this month. The Webb County listing puts the parasite's confirmed presence in Laredo's home county.

Pet and livestock owners should check animals daily for draining wounds, maggots or signs of discomfort, and call a veterinarian right away if they notice any of those signs, according to the report.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 18, 2026.
